objects.definition:
/** Handle for a FUSE filesystem */
struct fuse;
objects.description: Opaque handle representing a FUSE filesystem instance. Only forward-declared here; managed via API functions like fuse_new(), fuse_mount(), fuse_loop(), fuse_destroy().
Flags passed to ->readdir() to indicate readdir mode. FUSE_READDIR_PLUS requests attribute-prefilling (plus) mode.

objects.definition:
enum fuse_fill_dir_flags {
	/**
	 * "Plus" mode: file attributes are valid
	 *
	 * The attributes are used by the kernel to prefill the inode cache
	 * during a readdir.
	 *
	 * It is okay to set FUSE_FILL_DIR_PLUS if FUSE_READDIR_PLUS is not set
	 * and vice versa.
	 *
	 * This does not make libfuse honor the 'st_ino' field. That is
	 * controlled by the 'use_ino' option instead.
	 */
	FUSE_FILL_DIR_DEFAULTS = 0,
	FUSE_FILL_DIR_PLUS = (1 << 1)
};
objects.description: Flags passed to fuse_fill_dir_t callback to indicate validity of attributes for directory entries.
Callback type used by readdir implementations to add a directory entry to the userspace-provided buffer.

Configuration structure for the high-level FUSE API. Initialized from arguments in fuse_new() and may be adjusted in the filesystem init() handler. Contains caching, uid/gid/mode override policies, IO behaviors, and reserved fields for ABI stability.
Vector of callback function pointers that implement filesystem operations for a high-level FUSE filesystem.
Per-request context available during callbacks. Provides calling uid/gid/pid, pointer to the fuse handle, umask, and user private_data. Valid only during the operation.
Opaque stacking-API filesystem object representing a filesystem layer used with fuse_fs_* wrapper calls.

objects.definition:
typedef struct fuse_fs *(*fuse_module_factory_t)(struct fuse_args *args,
							 struct fuse_fs *fs[]);
objects.description: Function pointer type for module factories that construct fuse_fs instances, possibly using and consuming options from fuse_args.

objects.definition: typedef uint64_t fuse_ino_t;
objects.description: Inode number type used by the FUSE low-level API. It represents unique inode identifiers within the filesystem namespace. Underlying type is uint64_t.

objects.definition: typedef struct fuse_req *fuse_req_t;
objects.description: Opaque request handle used by handlers to reply to kernel requests. Valid only until a reply function is called for the request.

objects.definition: struct fuse_session;
objects.description: Opaque session object representing a FUSE connection/session. Used to mount, run loops, send notifications, and destroy a filesystem session.
Parameters describing a directory entry and its inode attributes, used in replies like fuse_reply_entry/create. Includes inode, generation, stat attrs, and cache timeouts.
Caller context attached to a request: uid, gid, pid, and umask. Retrieved via fuse_req_ctx() and only valid for the request lifetime.
Input item for forget_multi containing inode and lookup count to drop.
Callback set for custom I/O backends when using fuse_session_custom_io(). Provides read, writev and optional splice and clone_fd implementations for the session’s transport.
Flags controlling fuse_lowlevel_notify_entry/expire_entry behavior. 0 means invalidate, FUSE_LL_EXPIRE_ONLY requests expiry instead of immediate invalidation.

V-table of low-level FUSE filesystem operations implemented by the filesystem. Libfuse reads function pointers from this struct to dispatch incoming requests. New members are appended for ABI stability.

objects.definition: typedef void (*fuse_interrupt_func_t)(fuse_req_t req, void *data);
objects.description: Function pointer type for interrupt callbacks associated with a pending request.
Holds parsed common command-line options for low-level filesystems. Filled by fuse_parse_cmdline().

Holds configuration for a CUSE (Character device in Userspace) device. Includes major/minor numbers, an argv-style list of device info strings, and flags (e.g., CUSE_UNRESTRICTED_IOCTL). Used when creating/setting up a CUSE session.

Vtable of CUSE low-level operation callbacks. These are invoked by the framework to implement character device behavior (init, open, read/write, ioctl, etc.). Offsets and types mirror FUSE low-level ops but without inode numbers. Handlers must be provided by the user program as needed.

objects.definition: struct fuse_session;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a FUSE/CUSE session. Only a forward declaration is provided here; the full definition resides elsewhere. Used as the session object returned by cuse_lowlevel_* APIs.

Describes a single command-line option template and the action to take when it matches during FUSE option parsing. Supports setting a field by offset, invoking a processing callback via a key, or capturing a parameter into a target field based on the template format.
Holds a mutable, NULL-terminated vector of command-line arguments along with its count and an ownership flag. Used as both input and output for FUSE option parsing utilities.

objects.definition:
typedef int (*fuse_opt_proc_t)(void *data, const char *arg, int key,
			       struct fuse_args *outargs);
objects.description: Function pointer type for the option processing callback invoked by the parser when an argument matches certain conditions. Returns -1 on error, 0 to discard the arg, 1 to keep it.

Enumeration of log severity levels used by FUSE, aligned with syslog(2) priorities from most severe (EMERG) to least (DEBUG). Used to classify log messages throughout the library and by user-provided log handlers.

objects.definition:
typedef void (*fuse_log_func_t)(enum fuse_log_level level,
				const char *fmt, va_list ap);
objects.description: Function pointer type for custom log handlers. Implementations must be thread-safe and accept a severity level, a printf-style format string (including trailing newline), and a va_list of arguments. Installed via fuse_set_log_func to override default logging behavior.

functions.name: fuse_main_real_versioned
functions.signature: int fuse_main_real_versioned(int argc, char *argv[], const struct fuse_operations *op, size_t op_size, struct libfuse_version *version, void *user_data);
functions.description: Entry point that parses args, sets up the FUSE handle and event loop, using an explicit libfuse version record. Intended to be called by higher-level wrappers (e.g., fuse_main()). Returns 0 on success or a nonzero error code as documented by fuse_main().
requirements: argv must contain at least argv[0] (program name); argv[0] may be empty to suppress usage output.
op must point to a valid struct fuse_operations of size op_size.
version must point to a valid libfuse_version struct describing the desired ABI/API.
user_data is stored as initial fuse_context.private_data and may be overridden by operations.init.
Return codes follow the list described under fuse_main() documentation (1..7).

functions.name: fuse_main_real
functions.signature: static inline int fuse_main_real(int argc, char *argv[], const struct fuse_operations *op, size_t op_size, void *user_data);
functions.description: Internal convenience wrapper that warns (logs) that it is internal and forwards to fuse_main_real_versioned() with the current libfuse version. Prefer calling fuse_main() instead.
requirements: Same as fuse_main_real_versioned for argc/argv/op/op_size/user_data.
Caller should not rely on this as public API; use fuse_main().

functions.name: fuse_main_fn
functions.signature: static inline int fuse_main_fn(int argc, char *argv[], const struct fuse_operations *op, void *user_data);
functions.description: Public helper used by the fuse_main macro. Builds the current libfuse version and calls fuse_main_real_versioned() with op_size = sizeof(*op). Returns 0 on success, nonzero on failure.
requirements: argv must include argv[0] (program name); can be empty string to suppress usage.
op must be a valid pointer to a struct fuse_operations; sizeof(*op) is used to convey ABI size.
user_data becomes initial fuse_context.private_data (may be overridden by operations.init).

functions.name: fuse_main
functions.signature: int fuse_main(int argc, char *argv[], const struct fuse_operations *op, void *user_data);  /* implemented as a macro aliasing static inline int fuse_main_fn(int, char **, const struct fuse_operations *, void *) */
functions.description: Convenience entry point that initializes and runs a FUSE filesystem. It parses command-line options (including --help/--version), sets up signal handlers, creates the FUSE handle, registers the provided operations, and runs the single- or multi-threaded event loop. It returns 0 on success and a nonzero error code on failure (documented as 1..7). Although currently implemented as a macro mapping to fuse_main_fn(), it is the public API to call from main(). Typical usage is to prepare a fuse_operations instance, optionally parse custom options (e.g., via fuse_opt_parse), then call fuse_main(argc, argv, &ops, private_data). Notes: FUSE_USE_VERSION should be defined before including this header; argv[0] is used to construct usage text and may be an empty string to suppress it.
requirements: FUSE_USE_VERSION must be defined before including this header (per file header note).
argc/argv must represent the program’s command line; argv must have at least one element (argv[0]); argv[0] may be an empty string to suppress usage output.
op must point to a valid struct fuse_operations whose fields match the libfuse version being compiled against.
user_data sets the initial fuse_context::private_data; it may be overridden by the fuse_operations.init handler.

Return handling: caller should expect 0 on success; on failure, nonzero error codes may be: 1 (invalid option arguments), 2 (no mount point specified), 3 (FUSE setup failed), 4 (mounting failed), 5 (daemonize failure), 6 (signal handler setup failure), 7 (runtime filesystem error).
Do not call fuse_main_real() directly; fuse_main is the supported entry (note: fuse_main_real is internal).
Threading note: choosing single-threaded vs multi-threaded execution is handled internally based on options; if multi-threaded, callbacks must be thread-safe (see comments around fuse_loop_mt).

functions.name: fuse_lib_help
functions.signature: void fuse_lib_help(struct fuse_args *args);
functions.description: Prints a human-focused help text for available high- and low-level options to stdout. It may also locate and invoke help for additional modules referenced via module=foo options in args.
requirements: args must point to a valid fuse_args initialized with argument vector; it may be modified while discovering modules.

functions.name: _fuse_new_30
functions.signature: struct fuse *_fuse_new_30(struct fuse_args *args, const struct fuse_operations *op, size_t op_size, struct libfuse_version *version, void *user_data);
functions.description: Version-specific backend for creating a new FUSE handle (FUSE_USE_VERSION == 30). Used internally by fuse_new_fn().
requirements: args must contain argv with argv[0] present (program name semantics apply when parsing).
op must point to a valid struct fuse_operations; op_size must match the size for the compiled header ABI.
version must describe the desired libfuse version; provided by caller.
On unknown/invalid options, returns NULL and writes an error to stderr; on --help it prints help to stdout and returns NULL.

functions.name: _fuse_new_31
functions.signature: struct fuse *_fuse_new_31(struct fuse_args *args, const struct fuse_operations *op, size_t op_size, struct libfuse_version *version, void *user_data);
functions.description: Version-specific backend for creating a new FUSE handle (FUSE_USE_VERSION != 30 path). Used internally by fuse_new_fn().
requirements: Same as _fuse_new_30 regarding args/op/op_size/version semantics.
Returns a new struct fuse* on success; NULL on error or when --help is present.

functions.name: fuse_new_fn
functions.signature: static inline struct fuse *fuse_new_fn(struct fuse_args *args, const struct fuse_operations *op, size_t op_size, void *user_data);
functions.description: Inline wrapper selecting the appropriate _fuse_new_* implementation for the active FUSE_USE_VERSION. Returns a new FUSE handle or NULL (e.g., on --help or option error).
requirements: args must contain argv with argv[0] present; argv[0] may be empty to suppress usage in help output.
op must be valid and op_size must accurately reflect the struct layout at compile time.
user_data becomes initial fuse_context.private_data (may be overridden by operations.init).

functions.name: fuse_new
functions.signature: struct fuse *fuse_new(struct fuse_args *args, const struct fuse_operations *op, size_t op_size, void *user_data);  /* implemented as a macro aliasing static inline struct fuse *fuse_new_fn(struct fuse_args *, const struct fuse_operations *, size_t, void *) */
functions.description: Creates and returns a new FUSE handle after parsing generic and FUSE-specific mount options. On success, the handle can be mounted with fuse_mount() and driven with fuse_loop()/fuse_loop_mt(). If --help is present, it prints help to stdout and returns NULL. If unknown options are provided, it prints an error to stderr and returns NULL. Option parsing skips argv[0] (program name) when constructing help/usage. The provided fuse_operations are registered with the returned handle. Notes: FUSE_USE_VERSION should be defined before including this header; pass op_size equal to sizeof(*op) for the compilation target version.
requirements: FUSE_USE_VERSION must be defined before including this header (per file header note).
args must point to a valid struct fuse_args containing argc/argv; argv[0] must be present (may be empty string) and is skipped during option parsing for usage text.
op must point to a valid struct fuse_operations filled for the intended handlers; all methods are optional, but typical filesystems should at least implement getattr.
op_size must match the size of the struct fuse_operations used at compile time (recommended: sizeof(*op)).
user_data sets the initial fuse_context::private_data and may be overridden by the fuse_operations.init handler.
Error handling: returns NULL and prints help to stdout if --help is present; returns NULL and prints an error to stderr if an unknown option is provided.
Callers should not invoke the internal _fuse_new_30/_31 helpers directly; use fuse_new().
The returned struct fuse* must later be destroyed with fuse_destroy(); unmount with fuse_unmount() when needed (destroy does not unmount).

functions.name: fuse_mount
functions.signature: int fuse_mount(struct fuse *f, const char *mountpoint);
functions.description: Mounts the FUSE filesystem represented by handle f at the given mountpoint. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: f must be a valid FUSE handle created by fuse_new().
mountpoint must be a valid path to an existing mount point directory with appropriate permissions.
Caller must unmount via fuse_unmount() before destroying the handle.

functions.name: fuse_unmount
functions.signature: void fuse_unmount(struct fuse *f);
functions.description: Unmounts a FUSE filesystem previously mounted with fuse_mount(). See fuse_session_unmount() for additional details.
requirements: f must be a valid FUSE handle that is currently mounted.
Should be called before fuse_destroy() if the FS is still mounted.

functions.name: fuse_destroy
functions.signature: void fuse_destroy(struct fuse *f);
functions.description: Destroys and frees resources associated with the FUSE handle. Does not unmount; call fuse_unmount() first if needed.
requirements: f must be a valid FUSE handle or NULL. If not yet unmounted, caller should call fuse_unmount() before destroy.

functions.name: fuse_loop
functions.signature: int fuse_loop(struct fuse *f);
functions.description: Runs the single-threaded event loop, processing kernel requests and dispatching to registered operations until the session exits. Return value and exit conditions follow fuse_session_loop().
requirements: f must be a valid, mounted FUSE handle.
Operations registered in fuse_operations must be safe for recursive lookups in single-threaded mode.
Returns value as per fuse_session_loop(); caller should handle nonzero as error.

functions.name: fuse_exit
functions.signature: void fuse_exit(struct fuse *f);
functions.description: Signals the session to terminate. Causes any running event loop (single- or multi-threaded) to exit at the next opportunity.
requirements: f must be a valid FUSE handle.
Safe to call from callbacks or other threads to stop the loop.

functions.name: fuse_loop_mt_31
functions.signature: int fuse_loop_mt_31(struct fuse *f, int clone_fd);
functions.description: Multi-threaded event loop variant for older ABI (FUSE_USE_VERSION < 32). Processes requests in parallel. Signature accepts clone_fd (legacy parameter).
requirements: f must be a valid, mounted FUSE handle.
Callback code in fuse_operations must be thread-safe due to parallel invocation.
clone_fd usage/semantics are legacy; pass appropriate value for your platform (details not specified in this header).
Returns value as per fuse_session_loop().

functions.name: fuse_loop_mt_32
functions.signature: int fuse_loop_mt_32(struct fuse *f, struct fuse_loop_config *config);
functions.description: Multi-threaded event loop variant for mid ABI (FUSE_USE_VERSION < 3.12). Distributes requests across multiple threads based on config. Returns as per fuse_session_loop().
requirements: f must be a valid, mounted FUSE handle.
config may be NULL to use defaults; otherwise must point to a valid fuse_loop_config.
All registered operations must be thread-safe.

functions.name: fuse_loop_mt
functions.signature: int fuse_loop_mt(struct fuse *f, struct fuse_loop_config *config);
functions.description: Multi-threaded event loop entry point in current ABI. May be a real function (if built with versioned symbols) or a macro alias to an internal symbol. Processes requests in parallel across multiple threads.
requirements: f must be a valid, mounted FUSE handle.
config may be NULL to use defaults; otherwise provide a valid fuse_loop_config.
All filesystem callbacks must be thread-safe.
Return value semantics match fuse_session_loop().

functions.name: fuse_get_context
functions.signature: struct fuse_context *fuse_get_context(void);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the current request’s fuse_context, containing fuse handle, uid, gid, pid, private_data, and umask. Only valid during a filesystem operation callback.
requirements: Must be called only within the lifetime of a filesystem operation callback; the returned pointer must not be cached beyond the callback’s duration.

functions.name: fuse_getgroups
functions.signature: int fuse_getgroups(int size, gid_t list[]);
functions.description: Retrieves the supplementary group IDs for the current request’s calling thread. Returns total number of groups (even if larger than size) or -errno on failure; may return -ENOSYS if unsupported on the platform.
requirements: If size > 0, list must point to an array of at least size elements to receive group IDs.
Caller must handle return value > size by reallocating and retrying if full list is desired.
May parse /proc/$TID/task/$TID/status on Linux; not supported on all OSes.

functions.name: fuse_interrupted
functions.signature: int fuse_interrupted(void);
functions.description: Checks whether the current request has been interrupted. Returns 1 if interrupted, 0 otherwise.
requirements: Must be called in the context of handling a request to be meaningful.

functions.name: fuse_invalidate_path
functions.signature: int fuse_invalidate_path(struct fuse *f, const char *path);
functions.description: Invalidates kernel caches for the given path by calling the low-level invalidate inode notification. Returns 0 on success, negative error code otherwise. -ENOENT indicates there was nothing to invalidate (not an error).
requirements: f must be a valid FUSE handle.
path must be a valid, absolute or relative filesystem path known to the mounted filesystem.

functions.name: fuse_start_cleanup_thread
functions.signature: int fuse_start_cleanup_thread(struct fuse *fuse);
functions.description: Starts the background cleanup thread used with the "remember" option to prune inode/path caches. Automatically started by fuse_loop_mt(). Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: fuse must be a valid FUSE instance.
Typically only needed when using the remember option and not using fuse_loop_mt(). Avoid starting multiple times.

functions.name: fuse_stop_cleanup_thread
functions.signature: void fuse_stop_cleanup_thread(struct fuse *fuse);
functions.description: Stops the background cleanup thread associated with the "remember" option. Automatically managed by fuse_loop_mt().
requirements: fuse must be a valid FUSE instance.
Call only if you previously started the cleanup thread manually or are managing lifecycle explicitly.

functions.name: fuse_clean_cache
functions.signature: int fuse_clean_cache(struct fuse *fuse);
functions.description: Iterates over the internal cache and removes stale entries (used with -oremember). Returns the number of seconds until the next cleanup should be performed.
requirements: fuse must be a valid FUSE instance.
Intended to be used when manually managing cleanup (already done by standard sessions).

functions.name: fuse_fs_getattr
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_getattr(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, struct stat *buf, struct fuse_file_info *fi);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s getattr operation. Fills buf with attributes for path. Returns 0 on success or -errno on failure; -ENOSYS if not implemented.
requirements: fs must be a valid filesystem object.
path must reference an existing object.
buf must be a valid, writable pointer to struct stat.
fi may be NULL if file not open; otherwise must be valid.

functions.name: fuse_fs_rename
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_rename(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *oldpath, const char *newpath, unsigned int flags);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s rename operation from oldpath to newpath with flags (RENAME_EXCHANGE, RENAME_NOREPLACE).
requirements: fs must be valid.
oldpath and newpath must be valid paths.
If flags includes RENAME_NOREPLACE, newpath must not exist; otherwise return an error.
If flags includes RENAME_EXCHANGE, both paths must exist and must be exchanged atomically.

functions.name: fuse_fs_unlink
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_unlink(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s unlink (remove file) operation for path.
requirements: fs must be valid.
path must refer to a file (not directory).

functions.name: fuse_fs_rmdir
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_rmdir(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s rmdir (remove directory) operation for path.
requirements: fs must be valid.
path must refer to an empty directory.

functions.name: fuse_fs_symlink
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_symlink(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *linkname, const char *path);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s symlink operation to create a symlink at path pointing to linkname.
requirements: fs must be valid.
linkname is the target; path is the new symlink location and must not already exist.

functions.name: fuse_fs_link
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_link(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *oldpath, const char *newpath);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s link operation to create a hard link at newpath referencing oldpath.
requirements: fs must be valid.
oldpath must exist and be linkable; newpath must not exist.

functions.name: fuse_fs_release
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_release(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, struct fuse_file_info *fi);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s release (close) for an open file. Returns 0 (even if operation not defined).
requirements: fs must be valid.
fi must be the same handle as returned/used during open.
path may be NULL if the file was unlinked or directory removed after open (per directory note).

functions.name: fuse_fs_open
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_open(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, struct fuse_file_info *fi);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s open operation for path. May store a handle in fi->fh for later operations. Returns 0 (even if operation not defined).
requirements: fs must be valid.
path must exist and open flags are in fi->flags; fi must be a valid pointer.
Filesystem should check access unless default_permissions are in effect.

functions.name: fuse_fs_read
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_read(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, char *buf, size_t size, off_t off, struct fuse_file_info *fi);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s read operation to read size bytes at offset off into buf. Must return bytes read or -errno. With direct_io mount option, return value maps directly to read(2).
requirements: fs must be valid.
buf must point to a writable buffer of at least size bytes.
off must be >= 0.
fi must be valid if required by implementation.

functions.name: fuse_fs_read_buf
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_read_buf(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, struct fuse_bufvec **bufp, size_t size, off_t off, struct fuse_file_info *fi);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s read_buf operation. Returns data via a dynamically allocated fuse_bufvec stored at *bufp; memory will be freed by caller.
requirements: fs must be valid.
bufp must be non-NULL; the callee allocates a fuse_bufvec and assigns *bufp.
Any memory regions inside the buffer must be allocated with malloc(); caller frees them.
size is the requested size; off must be >= 0.

functions.name: fuse_fs_write
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_write(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, const char *buf, size_t size, off_t off, struct fuse_file_info *fi);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s write operation to write size bytes from buf at offset off. Returns bytes written or -errno. With direct_io, return maps directly to write(2).
requirements: fs must be valid.
buf must point to at least size bytes.
off must be >= 0.
Unless FUSE_CAP_HANDLE_KILLPRIV is disabled, filesystem is expected to clear setuid/setgid bits on write.

functions.name: fuse_fs_write_buf
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_write_buf(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, struct fuse_bufvec *buf, off_t off, struct fuse_file_info *fi);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s write_buf operation to write from a generic buffer vector at offset off. Use fuse_buf_copy() to move data to the destination.
requirements: fs must be valid.
buf must point to a valid fuse_bufvec describing the data.
off must be >= 0.
Unless FUSE_CAP_HANDLE_KILLPRIV is disabled, setuid/setgid bits are expected to be cleared on write.

functions.name: fuse_fs_fsync
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_fsync(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, int datasync, struct fuse_file_info *fi);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s fsync operation to synchronize file contents; if datasync != 0, only user data should be flushed, not metadata.
requirements: fs must be valid.
fi must refer to an open handle; path may be NULL if file removed after open.
datasync is a boolean-like flag as per fsync documentation.

functions.name: fuse_fs_flush
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_flush(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, struct fuse_file_info *fi);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s flush operation. May be called multiple times per open(). Errors may or may not be surfaced to userspace on close depending on platform.
requirements: fs must be valid.
fi must be valid and may be called multiple times per open().
Do not assume flush will always be called; it may be called more than expected or not at all.

functions.name: fuse_fs_statfs
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_statfs(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, struct statvfs *buf);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s statfs operation to get filesystem statistics. Some fields (f_favail, f_fsid, f_flag) are ignored by FUSE.
requirements: fs must be valid.
buf must be a writable pointer to struct statvfs.

functions.name: fuse_fs_opendir
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_opendir(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, struct fuse_file_info *fi);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s opendir operation. May store a directory handle in fi. Returns 0 (even if operation not defined).
requirements: fs must be valid.
path must refer to a directory.
Unless default_permissions is set, implementation should check permissions.

functions.name: fuse_fs_readdir
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_readdir(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, void *buf, fuse_fill_dir_t filler, off_t off, struct fuse_file_info *fi, enum fuse_readdir_flags flags);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s readdir operation to enumerate directory entries, invoking filler to add entries. Supports classic and PLUS modes; in PLUS mode, attributes provided may be used to prefill inode cache.
requirements: fs must be valid.
path must refer to a directory.
buf is the buffer passed to filler; filler must be used to append entries.
off may be 0 (no seeking support) or nonzero to support resuming.
If FUSE_READDIR_PLUS not set, only st_mode file type and (optionally) st_ino are used from provided stat.

functions.name: fuse_fs_fsyncdir
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_fsyncdir(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, int datasync, struct fuse_file_info *fi);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s fsyncdir to synchronize directory contents; if datasync != 0, only user data should be flushed.
requirements: fs must be valid.
path may be NULL if directory removed after opendir.
fi must be a valid directory handle.

functions.name: fuse_fs_releasedir
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_releasedir(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, struct fuse_file_info *fi);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s releasedir to close a directory handle. Returns 0 (even if operation not defined).
requirements: fs must be valid.
fi must be the directory handle returned by opendir.
path may be NULL if directory was removed after opendir.

functions.name: fuse_fs_create
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_create(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, mode_t mode, struct fuse_file_info *fi);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s create operation to create and open a file at path with mode, returning an open handle in fi.
requirements: fs must be valid.
path must not already exist; mode contains permission bits (type may be regular file).
fi must be valid and will receive an open handle if successful.

functions.name: fuse_fs_lock
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_lock(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, struct fuse_file_info *fi, int cmd, struct flock *lock);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s POSIX locking (fcntl) operation. cmd is F_GETLK, F_SETLK, or F_SETLKW; l_whence is always SEEK_SET. fi->owner should be used for lock ownership.
requirements: fs must be valid.
fi must be valid; fi->owner identifies the opener.
lock must point to a valid struct flock; l_whence will be SEEK_SET.
For F_GETLK, kernel may pre-check local locks; filesystem may fill l_pid or leave zero.

functions.name: fuse_fs_flock
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_flock(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, struct fuse_file_info *fi, int op);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s BSD flock operation with op being LOCK_SH, LOCK_EX, LOCK_UN (optionally ORed with LOCK_NB). fi->owner is unique per open and also provided to release().
requirements: fs must be valid.
fi must be valid and correspond to an open file.
op must be one of LOCK_SH, LOCK_EX, LOCK_UN optionally ORed with LOCK_NB.

functions.name: fuse_fs_chmod
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_chmod(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, mode_t mode, struct fuse_file_info *fi);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s chmod operation to change permission bits on path. fi may be NULL or an open handle.
requirements: fs must be valid.
mode contains the new permission bits.
fi may be NULL; if non-NULL must be valid.

functions.name: fuse_fs_chown
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_chown(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, uid_t uid, gid_t gid, struct fuse_file_info *fi);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s chown operation to change owner/group of path. Unless FUSE_CAP_HANDLE_KILLPRIV is disabled, expected to clear setuid/setgid bits.
requirements: fs must be valid.
uid and/or gid may be (implementation-defined) to indicate no change; both provided here.
fi may be NULL; if non-NULL must be valid.

functions.name: fuse_fs_truncate
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_truncate(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, off_t size, struct fuse_file_info *fi);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s truncate operation to change file size to size. Unless FUSE_CAP_HANDLE_KILLPRIV is disabled, expected to clear setuid/setgid bits.
requirements: fs must be valid.
size must be >= 0.
fi may be NULL; if non-NULL must be valid.

functions.name: fuse_fs_utimens
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_utimens(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, const struct timespec tv[2], struct fuse_file_info *fi);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s utimens operation to set access and modification times with nanosecond resolution. Supersedes utime().
requirements: fs must be valid.
tv must point to two timespecs (atime, mtime) as per utimensat(2).
fi may be NULL; if non-NULL must be valid.

functions.name: fuse_fs_access
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_access(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, int mask);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s access operation (for access(2)) to check permissions for path using mask.
requirements: fs must be valid.
mask is an access(2) mode mask.
If mounted with default_permissions, kernel pre-checks and this may not be called.

functions.name: fuse_fs_readlink
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_readlink(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, char *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s readlink operation. Fills buf with a NUL-terminated link target string, truncated if necessary. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: fs must be valid.
buf must be a writable buffer of length len; len includes space for the terminating NUL.

functions.name: fuse_fs_mknod
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_mknod(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, mode_t mode, dev_t rdev);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s mknod operation to create a non-directory, non-symlink node at path with mode and (for special files) rdev.
requirements: fs must be valid.
path must not already exist.
mode’s type bits should describe the node; for regular files create may be used instead.

functions.name: fuse_fs_mkdir
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_mkdir(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, mode_t mode);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s mkdir operation for path. Note: S_IFDIR type bits may need to be combined by the implementation (mode|S_IFDIR).
requirements: fs must be valid.
path must not already exist.
mode may lack S_IFDIR; implementation should set directory type bits appropriately.

functions.name: fuse_fs_setxattr
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_setxattr(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, const char *name, const char *value, size_t size, int flags);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s setxattr to set an extended attribute on path.
requirements: fs must be valid.
name must be a valid xattr name; value points to size bytes.
flags are as per setxattr(2) semantics.

functions.name: fuse_fs_getxattr
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_getxattr(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, const char *name, char *value, size_t size);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s getxattr to read an extended attribute value for name on path into value (up to size).
requirements: fs must be valid.
name must be a valid xattr name.
If size > 0, value must be a writable buffer of at least size bytes.

functions.name: fuse_fs_listxattr
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_listxattr(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, char *list, size_t size);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s listxattr to list attribute names on path into list buffer.
requirements: fs must be valid.
If size > 0, list must be a writable buffer of at least size bytes.

functions.name: fuse_fs_removexattr
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_removexattr(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, const char *name);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s removexattr to remove the named extended attribute from path.
requirements: fs must be valid.
name must be a valid xattr name present on path.

functions.name: fuse_fs_bmap
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_bmap(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, size_t blocksize, uint64_t *idx);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s bmap to map a file block index to an underlying device block index. Only meaningful for block-device-backed filesystems mounted with blkdev option.
requirements: fs must be valid.
blocksize is the block size used by the mapping.
idx must be a valid pointer to input/output block index.

functions.name: fuse_fs_ioctl
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_ioctl(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, unsigned int cmd, void *arg, struct fuse_file_info *fi, unsigned int flags, void *data);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s ioctl operation with the given command and data. Direction/size of data is determined by _IOC_* decoding of cmd; for _IOC_NONE data may be NULL; for _IOC_WRITE data is out area; for _IOC_READ data is in area; if both, data is in/out area. If flags has FUSE_IOCTL_DIR then fi refers to a directory handle. Note: the application’s unsigned long request is truncated to 32 bits.
requirements: fs must be valid.
cmd must be a valid ioctl command; note 32-bit truncation of request value.
arg, fi, data, and flags usage follow kernel/libfuse ioctl conventions.
If 32-bit compat on 64-bit, flags may include FUSE_IOCTL_COMPAT.

functions.name: fuse_fs_poll
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_poll(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, struct fuse_file_info *fi, struct fuse_pollhandle *ph, unsigned *reventsp);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s poll operation to report I/O readiness events. If ph is non-NULL, the client should notify events later via fuse_notify_poll(ph).
requirements: fs must be valid.
fi must refer to an open (possibly directory) handle.
ph may be NULL or a valid poll handle; callee is responsible for destroying ph with fuse_pollhandle_destroy() when no longer in use.
A single notification suffices to clear interest even if poll called multiple times with non-NULL ph.

functions.name: fuse_fs_fallocate
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_fallocate(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, int mode, off_t offset, off_t length, struct fuse_file_info *fi);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s fallocate to allocate space for a file region [offset, offset+length). On success, subsequent writes to that range will not fail due to lack of space.
requirements: fs must be valid.
offset and length must be >= 0.
mode contains fallocate mode flags as per posix_fallocate/fallocate semantics.
fi must refer to an open file handle.

functions.name: fuse_fs_copy_file_range
functions.signature: ssize_t fuse_fs_copy_file_range(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path_in, struct fuse_file_info *fi_in, off_t off_in, const char *path_out, struct fuse_file_info *fi_out, off_t off_out, size_t len, int flags);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s copy_file_range to perform an optimized in-kernel copy between two open files without shuttling data through userspace. If not implemented, applications should fall back to a regular copy.
requirements: fs must be valid.
fi_in and fi_out must refer to open file handles for path_in and path_out respectively.
off_in and off_out must be >= 0; len is the number of bytes to copy.
flags are reserved for future extensions (pass 0 unless documented otherwise).

functions.name: fuse_fs_lseek
functions.signature: off_t fuse_fs_lseek(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, off_t off, int whence, struct fuse_file_info *fi);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s lseek to find next data or hole or reposition file offset according to whence (e.g., SEEK_DATA/SEEK_HOLE if supported).
requirements: fs must be valid.
fi must refer to an open file handle; path may be provided for context.
off must be >= 0 when applicable; whence is one of SEEK_SET/SEEK_CUR/SEEK_END/SEEK_DATA/SEEK_HOLE.

functions.name: fuse_fs_statx
functions.signature: int fuse_fs_statx(struct fuse_fs *fs, const char *path, int flags, int mask, struct statx *stxbuf, struct fuse_file_info *fi);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s statx to get extended file attributes; fi may be NULL. If path is NULL, AT_EMPTY_PATH will already be set in flags.
requirements: fs must be valid.
stxbuf must be a writable pointer to struct statx.
flags/mask follow statx(2); if path is NULL, AT_EMPTY_PATH is set.
fi may be NULL or a valid open handle.

functions.name: fuse_fs_init
functions.signature: void fuse_fs_init(struct fuse_fs *fs, struct fuse_conn_info *conn, struct fuse_config *cfg);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s init hook, providing connection info and allowing the FS to adjust/validate the fuse_config.
requirements: fs must be valid.
conn must point to a valid fuse_conn_info structure supplied by libfuse.
cfg must point to a fuse_config that the FS may modify to ensure compatibility.

functions.name: fuse_fs_destroy
functions.signature: void fuse_fs_destroy(struct fuse_fs *fs);
functions.description: Calls the filesystem layer’s destroy hook for cleanup at filesystem exit.
requirements: fs must be valid (may be NULL if already cleaned up in some contexts).

functions.name: fuse_notify_poll
functions.signature: int fuse_notify_poll(struct fuse_pollhandle *ph);
functions.description: Notifies poll waiters registered via poll with a non-NULL poll handle that I/O readiness events occurred. One notification clears all outstanding interests.
requirements: ph must be a valid poll handle received in a prior poll callback.
Caller is responsible for lifecycle; destroy handle with fuse_pollhandle_destroy() when done.

functions.name: fuse_fs_new
functions.signature: struct fuse_fs *fuse_fs_new(const struct fuse_operations *op, size_t op_size, void *private_data);
functions.description: Creates a new fuse_fs stacking layer object for the provided operations. Typically used by modules to create a filesystem instance to push on a stack.
requirements: op must be a valid pointer to a struct fuse_operations; op_size must match its size for this ABI.
private_data will be used as initial fuse_context.private_data (may be overridden by operations.init).

functions.name: fuse_get_session
functions.signature: struct fuse_session *fuse_get_session(struct fuse *f);
functions.description: Returns the underlying session object associated with the FUSE handle.
requirements: f must be a valid FUSE handle.

functions.name: fuse_open_channel
functions.signature: int fuse_open_channel(const char *mountpoint, const char *options);
functions.description: Opens a FUSE file descriptor and sets up the mount for the given mountpoint and options. Returns the FUSE FD on success, or -1 on error.
requirements: mountpoint must reference an existing directory suitable as a mount point with proper privileges.
options is a mount-options string; must be valid for the platform’s mount helper.

functions.name: fuse_reply_err
functions.signature: int fuse_reply_err(fuse_req_t req, int err);
functions.description: Send a reply indicating success (err==0) or an error to a pending request. Applies to all requests except forget, forget_multi, and retrieve_reply. ENOSYS may have special meaning for some handlers as documented above.
requirements: req must be a valid outstanding request received by a low-level operation handler.
err must be a non-negative errno value (0 for success, positive error code for failure).
Caller should use documented errno values appropriate to the originating syscall semantics.
Do not call for forget, forget_multi, or retrieve_reply handlers (use fuse_reply_none instead).
After replying, the request handle becomes invalid and must not be reused.

functions.name: fuse_reply_none
functions.signature: void fuse_reply_none(fuse_req_t req);
functions.description: Indicate that no reply will be sent for a request. Intended for forget, forget_multi, and retrieve_reply.
requirements: Use only for requests that expect no reply: forget, forget_multi, retrieve_reply.
req must be a valid request handle from the corresponding callback.
Once called, req is consumed and must not be reused.

functions.name: fuse_reply_entry
functions.signature: int fuse_reply_entry(fuse_req_t req, const struct fuse_entry_param *e);
functions.description: Reply to operations that create or look up a directory entry (e.g., lookup, mknod, mkdir, symlink, link) with the entry parameters. On success, increases the entry’s lookup count.
requirements: req must be the request from lookup/mknod/mkdir/symlink/link.
e must point to a fully initialized fuse_entry_param. If e->ino is zero, this represents a negative entry (per documentation).
attr in e must be correct; FUSE may use attr.st_size for follow-up operations.
attr_timeout and entry_timeout should be set appropriately for caching semantics.
On success, lookup count is incremented by one; filesystem must eventually balance via forget.

functions.name: fuse_reply_create
functions.signature: int fuse_reply_create(fuse_req_t req, const struct fuse_entry_param *e, const struct fuse_file_info *fi);
functions.description: Reply to create with both a newly created entry and the open parameters. Increments the entry’s lookup count on success.
requirements: req must originate from the create handler.
e must describe the created node; same requirements as fuse_reply_entry regarding attr correctness and timeouts.
fi must contain fields used by the kernel: fh, direct_io, keep_cache, cache_readdir, nonseekable, noflush, parallel_direct_writes.
On success, lookup count is incremented; must be balanced via forget later.

functions.name: fuse_reply_attr
functions.signature: int fuse_reply_attr(fuse_req_t req, const struct stat *attr, double attr_timeout);
functions.description: Reply with inode attributes (e.g., for getattr/setattr).
requirements: req must be from getattr or setattr handlers.
attr must point to a valid struct stat and contain correct information (even if attr_timeout==0).
attr_timeout specifies validity in seconds; set appropriately for caching behavior.

functions.name: fuse_reply_readlink
functions.signature: int fuse_reply_readlink(fuse_req_t req, const char *link);
functions.description: Reply to readlink with the target path string.
requirements: req must be from readlink handler.
link must be a NUL-terminated string containing symlink contents.

functions.name: fuse_passthrough_open
functions.signature: int fuse_passthrough_open(fuse_req_t req, int fd);
functions.description: Associate a backing file descriptor with an open/opendir/create reply for passthrough I/O. Returns a positive backing id on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: Use during handling of open, opendir, or create requests before replying.
fd must be a valid open file descriptor for the backing file.
At most one backing id should exist per node/backing file (as noted).
Store/track returned backing id for later close via fuse_passthrough_close.

functions.name: fuse_passthrough_close
functions.signature: int fuse_passthrough_close(fuse_req_t req, int backing_id);
functions.description: Release a previously established passthrough backing association identified by backing_id.
requirements: backing_id must be the positive id returned by fuse_passthrough_open.
req must be a valid request context when closing passthrough; typically used in the same operation flow.

functions.name: fuse_reply_open
functions.signature: int fuse_reply_open(fuse_req_t req, const struct fuse_file_info *fi);
functions.description: Reply to open or opendir with open parameters (e.g., fh, direct_io, keep_cache, cache_readdir, nonseekable, noflush, parallel_direct_writes).
requirements: req must come from open or opendir handlers.
fi must be populated with relevant flags/fields for the kernel.
If FUSE_CAP_NO_OPEN_SUPPORT is negotiated and open/opendir handler is absent/returns ENOSYS, behavior may be auto-success; this function is for explicit replies.

functions.name: fuse_reply_write
functions.signature: int fuse_reply_write(fuse_req_t req, size_t count);
functions.description: Reply to write (or write_buf) indicating how many bytes were written.
requirements: req must be from write or write_buf handlers.
count must be the actual number of bytes written (can be less than requested on error conditions).

functions.name: fuse_reply_buf
functions.signature: int fuse_reply_buf(fuse_req_t req, const char *buf, size_t size);
functions.description: Reply with data bytes for read, readdir, getxattr, or listxattr. Copies from the provided memory buffer.
requirements: req must be from read, readdir, getxattr, or listxattr handlers.
buf must point to at least size bytes of readable memory; provide exactly requested byte counts unless EOF or documented exceptions (e.g., direct_io).
For getxattr/listxattr: adhere to size==0 and ERANGE semantics as described in corresponding handler docs.

functions.name: fuse_reply_data
functions.signature: int fuse_reply_data(fuse_req_t req, struct fuse_bufvec *bufv, enum fuse_buf_copy_flags flags);
functions.description: Reply with data from a buffer vector, potentially enabling zero-copy splicing per capability and flag rules. Used by read/readdir/getxattr/listxattr and readdirplus (increments lookup counts).
requirements: req must be from read, readdir, getxattr, listxattr, or readdirplus handlers.
bufv must describe the data; caller must ensure fields are valid. For write_buf, bufv->off must be maintained; for replies, ensure sizes align with request semantics.
flags control copy/splice; FUSE_BUF_NO_SPLICE disables splicing. SPLICE_F_MOVE requires corresponding capabilities and FUSE_BUF_SPLICE_MOVE flag.
When returning readdirplus data, this increments lookup count of each entry except '.' and '..' on success; filesystem must later balance via forget.

functions.name: fuse_reply_iov
functions.signature: int fuse_reply_iov(fuse_req_t req, const struct iovec *iov, int count);
functions.description: Reply with data from an array of iovec scatter-gather buffers for read, readdir, getxattr, or listxattr.
requirements: req must be from read, readdir, getxattr, or listxattr handlers.
iov must reference count valid buffers containing the reply data.

functions.name: fuse_reply_statfs
functions.signature: int fuse_reply_statfs(fuse_req_t req, const struct statvfs *stbuf);
functions.description: Reply to statfs with filesystem statistics.
requirements: req must be from statfs handler.
stbuf must point to a valid struct statvfs filled with correct stats.

functions.name: fuse_reply_xattr
functions.signature: int fuse_reply_xattr(fuse_req_t req, size_t count);
functions.description: Reply with the size needed for an xattr value or list when the caller provided size==0 (or when indicating required size).
requirements: req must be from getxattr or listxattr handlers.
count must be the required buffer size in bytes when size==0 was requested.

functions.name: fuse_reply_lock
functions.signature: int fuse_reply_lock(fuse_req_t req, const struct flock *lock);
functions.description: Reply to getlk with POSIX lock information.
requirements: req must be from getlk handler.
lock must describe the lock state to return.

functions.name: fuse_reply_bmap
functions.signature: int fuse_reply_bmap(fuse_req_t req, uint64_t idx);
functions.description: Reply to bmap with the device block index corresponding to the file block index.
requirements: req must be from bmap handler.
idx must be the mapped device block index.

functions.name: fuse_add_direntry
functions.signature: size_t fuse_add_direntry(fuse_req_t req, char *buf, size_t bufsize, const char *name, const struct stat *stbuf, off_t off);
functions.description: Format and append a single directory entry into a buffer for readdir. Returns the required space; if larger than bufsize, entry is not written.
requirements: buf must point to writable memory of size at least bufsize bytes.
name must be a NUL-terminated entry name.
stbuf must have st_ino and file type bits (mode bits 12-15) set; other fields are ignored.
off must be non-zero for subsequent entries; zero is reserved for 'from beginning' and should not be used for the first returned entry (pass offset of second entry instead).
Caller must compare return value to bufsize to detect insufficient space.

functions.name: fuse_add_direntry_plus
functions.signature: size_t fuse_add_direntry_plus(fuse_req_t req, char *buf, size_t bufsize, const char *name, const struct fuse_entry_param *e, off_t off);
functions.description: Format and append a directory entry with attributes for readdirplus. Returns required space; if larger than bufsize, no write occurs.
requirements: Same buffer and size rules as fuse_add_direntry.
name must be a NUL-terminated entry name.
e must be a valid fuse_entry_param with correct attr and timeouts.
off rules match fuse_add_direntry.

functions.name: fuse_reply_ioctl_retry
functions.signature: int fuse_reply_ioctl_retry(fuse_req_t req, const struct iovec *in_iov, size_t in_count, const struct iovec *out_iov, size_t out_count);
functions.description: Ask the kernel to retry the ioctl after fetching specified input data and preparing output buffers (for restricted/unrestricted ioctl flows).
requirements: req must be from ioctl handler.
in_iov/out_iov must reference valid user data locations for the retry per kernel expectations.
Use only when needing kernel to (re)setup in/out areas and resend ioctl.

functions.name: fuse_reply_ioctl
functions.signature: int fuse_reply_ioctl(fuse_req_t req, int result, const void *buf, size_t size);
functions.description: Complete an ioctl request with a result code and optional output buffer data.
requirements: req must be from ioctl handler.
result is the value to be returned to the caller.
If size>0, buf must point to at least size bytes of readable memory containing output.

functions.name: fuse_reply_ioctl_iov
functions.signature: int fuse_reply_ioctl_iov(fuse_req_t req, int result, const struct iovec *iov, int count);
functions.description: Complete an ioctl with scatter-gather output buffers.
requirements: req must be from ioctl handler.
iov must reference count valid buffers with output data.
result is the ioctl return value for the caller.

functions.name: fuse_reply_poll
functions.signature: int fuse_reply_poll(fuse_req_t req, unsigned revents);
functions.description: Reply to poll with a mask of ready events.
requirements: req must be from poll handler.
revents must be the bitmask of ready events for the file descriptor as per poll semantics.

functions.name: fuse_reply_lseek
functions.signature: int fuse_reply_lseek(fuse_req_t req, off_t off);
functions.description: Reply to lseek (SEEK_DATA/SEEK_HOLE) with the next offset.
requirements: req must be from lseek handler.
off is the resulting offset to return to the caller.

functions.name: fuse_reply_statx
functions.signature: int fuse_reply_statx(fuse_req_t req, int flags, struct statx *statx, double attr_timeout);
functions.description: Reply to statx with extended attributes and flags.
requirements: req must be from statx handler.
statx must point to a filled struct statx with requested fields as indicated by mask/flags in the request handler context.
attr_timeout controls attribute cache validity in seconds.

functions.name: fuse_lowlevel_notify_poll
functions.signature: int fuse_lowlevel_notify_poll(struct fuse_pollhandle *ph);
functions.description: Notify the kernel that IO readiness has changed for a previously registered poll handle (from poll handler).
requirements: ph must be a valid poll handle obtained from the poll handler invocation.
Caller must eventually destroy poll handles with fuse_pollhandle_destroy() when no longer needed (per poll docs).

functions.name: fuse_lowlevel_notify_inval_inode
functions.signature: int fuse_lowlevel_notify_inval_inode(struct fuse_session *se, fuse_ino_t ino, off_t off, off_t len);
functions.description: Invalidate cached data and/or attributes for an inode in the kernel. May trigger writeback before invalidation if writeback caching is enabled.
requirements: se must be a valid session.
Kernel must support protocol >= 7.12; otherwise returns -ENOSYS.
ino identifies target inode.
If off < 0, only attributes are invalidated; otherwise invalidate data from off for len bytes (len==0 means all).
May block if dirty pages exist; will not block if there are none.

functions.name: fuse_lowlevel_notify_increment_epoch
functions.signature: int fuse_lowlevel_notify_increment_epoch(struct fuse_session *se);
functions.description: Increment the connection epoch to invalidate caches validated against the prior epoch.
requirements: se must be a valid session.

functions.name: fuse_lowlevel_notify_inval_entry
functions.signature: int fuse_lowlevel_notify_inval_entry(struct fuse_session *se, fuse_ino_t parent, const char *name, size_t namelen);
functions.description: Invalidate parent attributes and the specified dentry in the kernel cache. When called correctly, it never blocks.
requirements: se must be a valid session.
Kernel must support protocol >= 7.12; otherwise returns -ENOSYS.
Must not be called in the execution path of related filesystem operations or while holding locks needed by such operations (see detailed list in comments).
parent must be a valid parent inode id.
name must point to the entry name and namelen must equal strlen(name).

functions.name: fuse_lowlevel_notify_expire_entry
functions.signature: int fuse_lowlevel_notify_expire_entry(struct fuse_session *se, fuse_ino_t parent, const char *name, size_t namelen);
functions.description: Mark a dentry as expired so the next access triggers a lookup instead of forceful removal. Preserves submounts unlike invalidation. Never blocks when called correctly.
requirements: se must be a valid session.
Kernel must support protocol >= 7.38; otherwise returns -ENOSYS.
Subject to the same call-path restrictions as fuse_lowlevel_notify_inval_entry (avoid deadlocks).
parent, name, namelen must specify the dentry; namelen must equal strlen(name).

functions.name: fuse_lowlevel_notify_delete
functions.signature: int fuse_lowlevel_notify_delete(struct fuse_session *se, fuse_ino_t parent, fuse_ino_t child, const char *name, size_t namelen);
functions.description: Invalidate a dentry like inval_entry, and if child matches the cached dentry’s inode, notify inotify watchers that it was deleted.
requirements: se must be a valid session.
Kernel must support protocol >= 7.18; otherwise returns -ENOSYS.
Must not be called on the execution path of a related filesystem operation or while holding conflicting locks (see comments).
parent and child must be valid inode numbers; name/namelen specify the dentry (namelen==strlen(name)).
When used correctly, the function does not block.

functions.name: fuse_lowlevel_notify_store
functions.signature: int fuse_lowlevel_notify_store(struct fuse_session *se, fuse_ino_t ino, off_t offset, struct fuse_bufvec *bufv, enum fuse_buf_copy_flags flags);
functions.description: Synchronously store data into the kernel’s page cache for the given inode and range, marking it up-to-date. May extend file size.
requirements: se must be a valid session; kernel must support protocol >= 7.15 or returns -ENOSYS.
ino identifies the target inode.
offset specifies starting offset; bufv must reference the data to store; flags control copy method.
If the operation fails, data may be partially stored.

functions.name: fuse_lowlevel_notify_retrieve
functions.signature: int fuse_lowlevel_notify_retrieve(struct fuse_session *se, fuse_ino_t ino, size_t size, off_t offset, void *cookie);
functions.description: Request that the kernel send back cached data for an inode range. On success, the filesystem’s retrieve_reply callback is invoked with the data.
requirements: se must be valid; kernel must support protocol >= 7.15 or returns -ENOSYS.
ino identifies the inode; size and offset specify the range to retrieve.
cookie is an opaque pointer returned to the retrieve_reply callback.
Only present pages are returned; retrieval stops at first non-present page.
On error, no reply is sent.

functions.name: fuse_req_userdata
functions.signature: void *fuse_req_userdata(fuse_req_t req);
functions.description: Return the userdata pointer that was supplied to fuse_session_new() for the session handling this request.
requirements: req must be a valid request handle.

functions.name: fuse_req_ctx
functions.signature: const struct fuse_ctx *fuse_req_ctx(fuse_req_t req);
functions.description: Return the per-request context (uid, gid, pid, umask). Pointer is valid only for the lifetime of the request.
requirements: req must be valid; caller must not retain the returned pointer beyond the request lifetime.

functions.name: fuse_req_getgroups
functions.signature: int fuse_req_getgroups(fuse_req_t req, int size, gid_t list[]);
functions.description: Retrieve the calling process’s supplementary group IDs for the request. Returns the total number of groups (even if larger than size), or -errno. May return -ENOSYS on platforms without support.
requirements: req must be valid.
If size>0, list must point to an array of at least size elements to be filled.
Caller must handle return value > size by reallocating and retrying if needed.
On some systems, may parse /proc/.../status; feature may be unsupported (-ENOSYS).

functions.name: fuse_req_interrupt_func
functions.signature: void fuse_req_interrupt_func(fuse_req_t req, fuse_interrupt_func_t func, void *data);
functions.description: Register or unregister a callback to be invoked if the request gets interrupted. If an interrupt already occurred, the callback may be invoked from within this function.
requirements: req must be a valid outstanding request.
func may be NULL to unregister; otherwise must be a valid function pointer.
data is user pointer passed to the callback.

functions.name: fuse_req_interrupted
functions.signature: int fuse_req_interrupted(fuse_req_t req);
functions.description: Check whether the given request has already been interrupted. Returns 1 if interrupted, 0 otherwise.
requirements: req must be a valid request handle.

functions.name: fuse_lowlevel_version
functions.signature: void fuse_lowlevel_version(void);
functions.description: Print low-level libfuse version information to stdout.
requirements: No arguments; prints to stdout.

functions.name: fuse_lowlevel_help
functions.signature: void fuse_lowlevel_help(void);
functions.description: Print available low-level options of interest to end users to stdout (not exhaustive).
requirements: No arguments; prints to stdout.

functions.name: fuse_cmdline_help
functions.signature: void fuse_cmdline_help(void);
functions.description: Print available options for fuse_parse_cmdline() to stdout.
requirements: No arguments; prints to stdout.

functions.name: fuse_parse_cmdline
functions.signature: int fuse_parse_cmdline(struct fuse_args *args, struct fuse_cmdline_opts *opts);
functions.description: Parse common command-line options for low-level filesystems. Removes known options from args, sets opts. Prints help/version on request.
requirements: args must point to an initialized fuse_args (argv-style) with argv[0] present.
opts must be a valid output struct pointer.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
Leaves unknown options in args. Adds a subtype if neither -o subtype nor -o fsname provided.

functions.name: fuse_session_new_versioned
functions.signature: struct fuse_session *fuse_session_new_versioned(struct fuse_args *args, const struct fuse_lowlevel_ops *op, size_t op_size, struct libfuse_version *version, void *userdata);
functions.description: Create a low-level session using the provided operations table and version information. Returns a session for mounting and looping.
requirements: args must be initialized; argv[0] must be present (may be empty string).
op may be NULL to create a no-op session; otherwise must point to a struct fuse_lowlevel_ops of size op_size.
version must describe the libfuse version the FS was compiled against.
userdata is stored and retrievable via fuse_req_userdata.
Parses mount options; on unknown/invalid options prints error to stderr and returns NULL.

functions.name: fuse_session_custom_io_317
functions.signature: int fuse_session_custom_io_317(struct fuse_session *se, const struct fuse_custom_io *io, size_t op_size, int fd);
functions.description: Set a custom I/O interface and file descriptor for a session (3.17+ underlying entry point). Enables using a custom transport instead of mountpoint operations.
requirements: se must be a valid session.
io must be non-NULL; io->read and io->writev MUST be provided; splice_send/receive optional; clone_fd optional.
op_size must reflect the size of struct fuse_custom_io supported by the caller (used for ABI sizing).
fd must be >=0 and is closed by fuse_session_destroy().
Returns 0 on success; returns -EINVAL if io or required members are NULL; -EBADF if fd<0; -errno on allocation failure.

functions.name: fuse_session_custom_io
functions.signature: static inline int fuse_session_custom_io(struct fuse_session *se, const struct fuse_custom_io *io, size_t op_size, int fd);
functions.description: Inline wrapper that forwards to fuse_session_custom_io_317 on libfuse >= 3.17 to set custom I/O for a session.
requirements: Same requirements as fuse_session_custom_io_317: non-NULL io with read and writev set; valid se; fd >= 0; op_size must match provided struct size.

functions.name: fuse_session_mount
functions.signature: int fuse_session_mount(struct fuse_session *se, const char *mountpoint);
functions.description: Mount the FUSE filesystem at the provided mountpoint for the given session.
requirements: se must be a valid session created by fuse_session_new().
mountpoint must be a valid path string.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: fuse_session_loop
functions.signature: int fuse_session_loop(struct fuse_session *se);
functions.description: Enter a single-threaded, blocking event loop processing FUSE requests until the connection closes or session is exited. Returns 0 on normal disconnect, -errno on processing error, or a positive signal number if terminated by a signal installed via fuse_set_signal_handlers().
requirements: se must be a mounted, valid session.
Caller should check mount state after return to distinguish regular unmount versus connection abort via sysfs.

functions.name: fuse_session_loop_mt
functions.signature: int fuse_session_loop_mt(struct fuse_session *se, struct fuse_loop_config *config);
functions.description: Enter a multi-threaded event loop. Return semantics mirror fuse_session_loop().
requirements: se must be a mounted, valid session.
config must point to a valid fuse_loop_config structure (fields per libfuse version).

functions.name: fuse_session_exit
functions.signature: void fuse_session_exit(struct fuse_session *se);
functions.description: Mark the session as terminated so event loops exit at the next opportunity. For non-worker threads, exit occurs upon next received request unless woken with a signal.
requirements: se must be a valid session.
To wake a blocking main thread when using fuse_set_signal_handlers(), sending SIGPIPE can trigger wake-up without side effects.

functions.name: fuse_session_reset
functions.signature: void fuse_session_reset(struct fuse_session *se);
functions.description: Reset the session’s terminated flag.
requirements: se must be a valid session.

functions.name: fuse_session_exited
functions.signature: int fuse_session_exited(struct fuse_session *se);
functions.description: Query if the session has been flagged as exited. Returns 1 if exited, 0 otherwise.
requirements: se must be a valid session.

functions.name: fuse_session_unmount
functions.signature: void fuse_session_unmount(struct fuse_session *se);
functions.description: Ensure the filesystem is unmounted and the kernel communication channel is closed if still open. Does almost nothing if the kernel already closed the channel.
requirements: se must be a valid session.
Does not unmount if the kernel connection was aborted via /sys/.../abort (by design).

functions.name: fuse_session_destroy
functions.signature: void fuse_session_destroy(struct fuse_session *se);
functions.description: Destroy a session and free associated resources. Closes custom I/O file descriptor if set.
requirements: se must be a valid session pointer (may be NULL-safe depending on implementation, not specified here).
Should be called after unmounting/loop exit to release resources.

functions.name: fuse_session_fd
functions.signature: int fuse_session_fd(struct fuse_session *se);
functions.description: Return the file descriptor used for communication with the kernel, for integrating with custom event loops.
requirements: se must be a valid session.
Returned fd remains valid until fuse_session_unmount().

functions.name: fuse_session_process_buf
functions.signature: void fuse_session_process_buf(struct fuse_session *se, const struct fuse_buf *buf);
functions.description: Process a raw FUSE request supplied in a fuse_buf (memory buffer or pipe FD). Use with custom event loops after fuse_session_receive_buf.
requirements: se must be a valid session.
buf must describe a received raw request previously read from the session.

functions.name: fuse_session_receive_buf
functions.signature: int fuse_session_receive_buf(struct fuse_session *se, struct fuse_buf *buf);
functions.description: Read a raw request from the kernel into the provided fuse_buf. May read into memory or splice into a temporary pipe depending on configuration and size.
requirements: se must be a valid session.
buf must point to a fuse_buf to be filled. Caller must handle return value as the actual request size or -errno on error.

functions.name: fuse_req_is_uring
functions.signature: bool fuse_req_is_uring(fuse_req_t req);
functions.description: Check whether the request was submitted through fuse-io-uring.
requirements: req must be a valid request handle.

functions.name: fuse_req_get_payload
functions.signature: int fuse_req_get_payload(fuse_req_t req, char **payload, size_t *payload_sz, void **mr);
functions.description: Obtain a writable payload buffer for a request submitted via fuse-io-uring so the filesystem can write output directly, avoiding extra copies.
requirements: req must be a valid request originating from fuse-io-uring; otherwise returns -errno.
payload and payload_sz must be non-NULL output pointers.
mr is a memory registration handle (currently unused) and may be NULL if not needed.
Returns 0 on success, -errno on failure.

functions.name: cuse_lowlevel_new
functions.signature: struct fuse_session *cuse_lowlevel_new(struct fuse_args *args, const struct cuse_info *ci, const struct cuse_lowlevel_ops *clop, void *userdata);
functions.description: Create and initialize a CUSE (Character device in Userspace) low-level session using provided command-line style arguments, device information, and operation callbacks. Typically used to set up a session object that can later be attached/run by the caller. Returns a session handle on success. Exact error/return conventions are not documented here; by FUSE/CUSE convention, NULL is returned on failure. The function does not start the event loop; it only constructs the session.
requirements: args must point to a valid struct fuse_args if non-NULL; any embedded pointers must remain valid for the lifetime of the created session or until explicitly copied by the library (not specified here).
ci must point to a valid struct cuse_info; any strings referenced by ci->dev_info_argv must be valid, and counts (dev_info_argc) must correctly match the array length.

clop must point to a valid struct cuse_lowlevel_ops; any function pointers provided will be called by the framework and must conform to the expected signatures. Unspecified which callbacks are mandatory.
userdata is an opaque pointer passed back to callbacks; if used, it must remain valid for the lifetime of the session.
Caller should check the returned pointer for NULL to detect initialization failure (inferred from common FUSE patterns).
The created session must later be properly torn down using an appropriate teardown/destroy API to avoid resource leaks (inferred).

functions.name: cuse_lowlevel_setup
functions.signature: struct fuse_session *cuse_lowlevel_setup(int argc, char *argv[], const struct cuse_info *ci, const struct cuse_lowlevel_ops *clop, int *multithreaded, void *userdata);
functions.description: Parse command-line arguments and set up a CUSE low-level session in one step, returning a session handle and optionally indicating threading mode via the multithreaded out-parameter. This is a convenience wrapper around session creation and configuration; it does not document whether it also starts the session loop. Return value/error behavior is not explicitly described; by convention, NULL indicates failure.
requirements: argc must be the number of elements in argv and must be non-negative.
argv must point to an array of at least argc pointers to null-terminated strings; each string must remain valid during setup.
ci must point to a valid struct cuse_info with consistent fields (e.g., dev_info_argc matches the number of entries in dev_info_argv).
clop must point to a valid struct cuse_lowlevel_ops; callback lifetimes must extend through the session’s lifetime.
multithreaded, if non-NULL, must point to an int location writable by the function (used to report threading mode; exact semantics unknown).
userdata is an opaque pointer passed back during callbacks and must remain valid for the session lifetime.
Caller should check the returned session pointer for NULL to detect setup failure (inferred from common FUSE patterns).
The returned session must be later torn down with cuse_lowlevel_teardown or equivalent to release resources (inferred).

functions.name: cuse_lowlevel_teardown
functions.signature: void cuse_lowlevel_teardown(struct fuse_session *se);
functions.description: Tear down and clean up a previously created CUSE low-level session, releasing resources associated with the session handle. Intended to be called once when the session is no longer needed.
requirements: se must be a valid pointer to a struct fuse_session previously obtained from cuse_lowlevel_new or cuse_lowlevel_setup.
se must not have been previously torn down; calling more than once is undefined (inferred).
After this call returns, the session handle must not be used again (inferred).
Must not be called concurrently with active callbacks or while the session is still running/servicing requests (inferred).

functions.name: cuse_lowlevel_main
functions.signature: int cuse_lowlevel_main(int argc, char *argv[], const struct cuse_info *ci, const struct cuse_lowlevel_ops *clop, void *userdata);
functions.description: Convenience entry point that sets up and runs a CUSE low-level session using command-line arguments, device info, and operation callbacks, blocking until termination. Returns a process-style status code; specific success/error values are not defined here.
requirements: argc must be the number of elements in argv and must be non-negative.
argv must point to an array of at least argc pointers to null-terminated strings valid for the duration of setup.
ci must point to a valid struct cuse_info with consistent fields (dev_major/dev_minor, dev_info_argc/dev_info_argv, flags).
clop must point to a valid struct cuse_lowlevel_ops; provided callbacks must be valid and remain available while the session is running.
userdata is an opaque pointer passed to callbacks and must remain valid for the duration of the run.
Caller should check the returned int for non-zero to detect failure; exact return conventions are unspecified (unknown).

functions.name: fuse_opt_parse
functions.signature: int fuse_opt_parse(struct fuse_args *args, void *data, const struct fuse_opt opts[], fuse_opt_proc_t proc);
functions.description: Parses command-line style options in args against an array of fuse_opt templates, applying actions (set variables, invoke callback, or assign option parameters) and building an output argument list. Intended to normalize/handle FUSE options and optionally keep or discard arguments via a user-supplied processing callback. NULL is permitted for args (treated as an empty vector), for opts (treated as a single end marker), and for proc (treated as an always-keep callback).
requirements: args may be NULL to represent an empty argument vector; otherwise it should reference a valid/initialized struct fuse_args (e.g., via FUSE_ARGS_INIT or returned by a previous fuse_opt_parse)
data is user-defined and may be NULL; it is passed through to proc
opts may be NULL; otherwise it must be a valid array of struct fuse_opt terminated by FUSE_OPT_END (templ == NULL)
proc may be NULL; otherwise it must be a function compatible with fuse_opt_proc_t and must return -1 on error, 0 to discard, or 1 to keep the argument
If a fuse_opt entry uses action iii) for strings (format %s), the destination char* pointed to by offset will be freed if non-NULL and replaced with an allocated copy
For two-argument options (e.g., "-x foo"), callers should expect the parser to normalize them to single-argument form ("-xfoo") before proc is called
Options of the form "-ofoo" are passed to proc without the "-o" prefix
Return value -1 indicates an error during parsing or callback; 0 indicates success

functions.name: fuse_opt_add_opt
functions.signature: int fuse_opt_add_opt(char **opts, const char *opt);
functions.description: Appends opt to a comma-separated option list string referenced by *opts, allocating or resizing as needed. If *opts is NULL, creates a new list containing opt. Does not escape commas; use fuse_opt_add_opt_escaped for that behavior.
requirements: opts must be a valid pointer to a char* variable; *opts may be NULL
opt must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string
On allocation failure, returns -1 and leaves *opts unchanged or set to a valid state (caller must check return value)
On success returns 0 and may allocate or reallocate memory for *opts; caller is responsible for freeing the resulting string when no longer needed (ownership remains with caller)

functions.name: fuse_opt_add_opt_escaped
functions.signature: int fuse_opt_add_opt_escaped(char **opts, const char *opt);
functions.description: Appends opt to a comma-separated option list like fuse_opt_add_opt, but escapes commas in opt so the resulting list remains parseable as single options.
requirements: opts must be a valid pointer to a char* variable; *opts may be NULL
opt must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string
On allocation failure, returns -1; caller must check return value
On success returns 0 and may allocate or reallocate memory for *opts; caller is responsible for freeing the resulting string when no longer needed

functions.name: fuse_opt_add_arg
