functions.signature: int fuse_opt_add_arg(struct fuse_args *args, const char *arg);
functions.description: Appends a new argument string to the NULL-terminated argv vector inside args, updating argc and reallocating as needed.
requirements: args must point to a valid/initialized struct fuse_args (e.g., via FUSE_ARGS_INIT or returned by previous API calls)
arg must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string
On allocation failure, returns -1; caller must check return value
On success returns 0; args->argv remains NULL-terminated after insertion

functions.name: fuse_opt_insert_arg
functions.signature: int fuse_opt_insert_arg(struct fuse_args *args, int pos, const char *arg);
functions.description: Inserts a new argument string at position pos within the NULL-terminated argv vector in args, shifting subsequent entries. Useful for placing options before the special "--" argument.
requirements: args must point to a valid/initialized struct fuse_args
arg must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string
pos must be within the range 0..args->argc (inserting at args->argc is equivalent to appending)
On allocation failure, returns -1; caller must check return value
On success returns 0; args->argv remains NULL-terminated and args->argc is updated

functions.name: fuse_opt_free_args
functions.signature: void fuse_opt_free_args(struct fuse_args *args);
functions.description: Frees any memory owned by the contents of a struct fuse_args (e.g., argv entries and vector) without freeing the struct itself. Use when the argument list is no longer needed.
requirements: args must point to a valid struct fuse_args (may be zeroed/initialized even if empty)
The function frees only the contents; the struct fuse_args itself remains allocated and owned by the caller
After calling, args fields may be reset/cleared by the implementation; caller should not use any previously returned argv pointers

functions.name: fuse_opt_match
functions.signature: int fuse_opt_match(const struct fuse_opt opts[], const char *opt);
functions.description: Checks whether the string opt matches any template in a fuse_opt array according to FUSE's option matching rules. Returns 1 if a match is found, 0 otherwise.
requirements: opts must be a valid array of struct fuse_opt terminated by FUSE_OPT_END (templ == NULL)
opt must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string
Return value is 1 for a match, 0 for no match

functions.name: fuse_set_log_func
functions.signature: void fuse_set_log_func(fuse_log_func_t func);
functions.description: Install or reset the global libfuse log message handler. When set, all subsequent libfuse log messages are routed to the provided thread-safe callback instead of the default destination (stderr or syslog if enabled). Pass NULL to revert to the default handler. The handler may be invoked from any libfuse function, including during early initialization before a filesystem is created.
requirements: func must be a valid function pointer of type fuse_log_func_t or NULL.
If func is non-NULL, the callback must be thread-safe (it may be called from any thread and from any libfuse function, including before a filesystem is created).
The installed handler is global for the process and affects all FUSE filesystems created within the process.
The handler must correctly handle a printf-style format string and a va_list (do not reuse the va_list after it has been consumed unless you copy it per va_copy rules).

functions.name: fuse_log
functions.signature: void fuse_log(enum fuse_log_level level, const char *fmt, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
functions.description: Emit a log message at the given severity level through the current libfuse logging backend (default stderr, custom handler if installed, or syslog if enabled). Uses printf-style formatting with variable arguments.
requirements: level must be a valid value of enum fuse_log_level (e.g., FUSE_LOG_ERR, FUSE_LOG_DEBUG).
fmt must be a non-NULL printf-style format string and should include a trailing newline as documented.
The variable arguments must match the format specifiers in fmt (GCC/Clang format checking applies via the format attribute).
May be called at any time; no FUSE filesystem needs to be created.

functions.name: fuse_log_enable_syslog
functions.signature: void fuse_log_enable_syslog(const char *ident, int option, int facility);
functions.description: Switch the default libfuse log handler from stderr to syslog, using parameters analogous to openlog(3). After calling this, libfuse log messages are sent to syslog unless a custom handler is installed later.
requirements: ident, option, and facility must be suitable for openlog(3); option and facility should be composed of valid LOG_* flags for the platform.
If syslog logging is enabled for the process, fuse_log_close_syslog() should be called at teardown to close the syslog connection.
This changes the global log backend for the process.

functions.name: fuse_log_close_syslog
functions.signature: void fuse_log_close_syslog(void);
functions.description: Close the syslog connection previously enabled by fuse_log_enable_syslog(). Intended to be called during teardown/cleanup.
requirements: Call after fuse_log_enable_syslog() when syslog logging is no longer needed (typically at process or library teardown).
Safe to call in teardown context; other ordering constraints are not specified.

import os
import random
import struct
import zlib

# Generator for arbitrary binary data inputs tailored to libfuse fuzz stubs that
# consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM (ints), especially for:
# - file paths (strings)
# - write payloads (binary, capped sizes)
# - ioctl data areas (binary)
# - argv/option strings for fuse_args and fuse_opt APIs
# - identifiers for syslog/logging
#
# Strategy:
# - Create a compact container that concatenates several length-prefixed blobs
#   the harness will draw from via FUZZ_PARAM_STR in order. We interleave these
#   with integers encoded little-endian so FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) and FUZZ_PARAM(int)
#   can read plausible values from the same stream.
# - Include a mixture of realistic UNIX paths, options, and binary payloads.
# - Keep total output <= 4096 bytes.
#
# Container layout (all little-endian):
# [magic 4B]
# repeated entries until size limit:
#   [tag 1B]
#   if tag in {0x01 string, 0x02 bin}:
#       [len 2B] [data len bytes]
#   if tag in {0x10 uint32, 0x11 int32}:
#       [value 4B]
# End with checksum [CRC32 4B] of all preceding bytes to make buffers non-random but valid.
# The fuzzer infra will not parse this format; we simply provide a rich sequence so successive
# FUZZ_PARAM_* calls return diverse data.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

REALISTIC_PATHS = [
    b"/file",
    b"/dir/sub/file.txt",
    b"/tmp/fuzz.bin",
    b"/var/log/fuse.log",
    b"/dev/null",
    b"/home/user/data",
    b"/mnt/test/alpha",
    b"/a",
]

# Option snippets to exercise fuse_opt_* and fuse_main paths
OPTION_SNIPPETS = [
    b"--help",
    b"--version",
    b"-d",
    b"--num=123",
    b"--name=fuse",
    b"-o allow_other",
    b"-o subtype=fuzz",
    b"-o fsname=fuzzfs",
    b"--key",
]

# Strings with commas to test fuse_opt_add_opt_escaped
ESCAPED_OPTS = [
    b"opt,with,commas",
    b"a,b,c=d,e",
]

# Syslog ident like values
IDENTS = [b"fuzzfs", b"cuse", b"libfuse", b"test"]

# Binary payload makers

def rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def make_payloads(rng: random.Random):
    # A mix of textual and binary payloads to be consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    payloads = []

    # Realistic paths (some empty allowed for defaulting in stubs)
    paths = REALISTIC_PATHS[:]
    rng.shuffle(paths)
    payloads.extend(paths[: rng.randint(3, min(6, len(paths)))])

    # Some empty string entries to trigger defaults in stubs
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 2)):
        payloads.append(b"")

    # Option strings and argv-like tokens
    opts = OPTION_SNIPPETS[:]
    rng.shuffle(opts)
    payloads.extend(opts[: rng.randint(3, min(7, len(opts)))])

    # Escaped options
    payloads.extend(ESCAPED_OPTS)

    # Logging messages
    msgs = [
        b"hello world",
        b"value=%d hex=%x",
        b"pi=3.141 name=fuse num=42",
        b"literal message",
    ]
    payloads.extend(msgs)

    # Write/ioctl binary payloads with varying sizes
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 6)):
        sz = rng.choice([1, 7, 32, 128, 256, 512, 800, 1000])
        sz = min(sz, 1024)  # caps aligning with stubs
        # Mix printable and random bytes
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            data = (b"ABCD" * ((sz // 4) + 1))[:sz]
        else:
            data = rand_bytes(rng, sz)
        payloads.append(data)

    # Short names for argv[0]
    payloads.append(rng.choice(IDENTS))

    return payloads


def pack_entry(tag: int, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    if tag in (0x01, 0x02):
        ln = len(data)
        if ln > 0xFFFF:
            data = data[:0xFFFF]
            ln = len(data)
        return bytes([tag]) + struct.pack('<H', ln) + data
    elif tag in (0x10, 0x11):
        return bytes([tag]) + data  # data must be 4 bytes
    else:
        return b""


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    chunks = []
    chunks.append(b"FUZ3")  # magic

    # Build a stream interleaving strings/binaries and integers
    payloads = make_payloads(rng)

    # Pre-generate a set of integers to be consumed by FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)/int
    ints = []
    for _ in range(40):
        # Include values that stubs mod by, offsets, sizes, flags
        val = rng.getrandbits(32)
        # Occasionally force small bounded values useful for flags/levels
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            val = rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 31, 63, 255, 1024, 4096, (1 << 18) - 1])
        ints.append(val)

    # Interleave entries until near limit
    i_payload = 0
    i_int = 0
    # Ensure at least one non-empty payload for store/reply paths
    non_empty_added = False

    def can_add(n: int) -> bool:
        return sum(len(c) for c in chunks) + n + 4 <= MAX_TOTAL  # +4 for CRC later

    while (i_payload < len(payloads) or i_int < len(ints)) and sum(len(c) for c in chunks) < (MAX_TOTAL - 8):
        choice = rng.random()
        if (i_payload < len(payloads) and (choice < 0.6 or i_int >= len(ints))):
            data = payloads[i_payload]
            i_payload += 1
            tag = 0x01  # treat all FUZZ_PARAM_STR sources similarly
            entry = pack_entry(tag, data)
            if can_add(len(entry)):
                chunks.append(entry)
                if len(data) > 0:
                    non_empty_added = True
            else:
                break
        else:
            # Integer entry
            val = ints[i_int]
            i_int += 1
            # Randomly pick signed or unsigned
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                tag = 0x10
                entry = pack_entry(tag, struct.pack('<I', val))
            else:
                tag = 0x11
                entry = pack_entry(tag, struct.pack('<i', struct.unpack('<i', struct.pack('<I', val))[0]))
            if can_add(len(entry)):
                chunks.append(entry)
            else:
                break

    # If we didn't add any non-empty payload, force a small one for correctness
    if not non_empty_added:
        data = b"x"
        entry = pack_entry(0x01, data)
        if can_add(len(entry)):
            chunks.append(entry)

    body = b"".join(chunks)
    crc = zlib.crc32(body) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    body += struct.pack('<I', crc)
    # Ensure size bound
    return body[:MAX_TOTAL]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets libfuse stubs that request:
# - path strings (FUZZ_PARAM_STR)
# - xattr name tails consisting of [A-Za-z0-9_.-]
# - xattr values (arbitrary bytes but kept small)
# - sizes/flags via FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)
# - directory entry names without '/' and control chars
# - inode numbers via FUZZ_PARAM(uint64_t)
#
# The fuzzer framework will draw multiple FUZZ_PARAM_* from a single
# provided buffer. We therefore pack a sequence of length-prefixed fields
# to satisfy calls in the stubs in a valid and interesting way.
#
# Encoding format (little-endian):
#   - 32-bit LE count N of subsequent fields
#   - Then N fields, each:
#       * 8-bit type tag:
#           0x01 = string (len16 + data)
#           0x02 = u32     (4 bytes)
#           0x03 = u64     (8 bytes)
#       * payload per type
#
# We include fields in an order that matches common consumption in the
# provided stubs:
#  For xattr ops (set/get/remove):
#   - path string (non-empty, starts with '/')
#   - xattr tail identifier (allowed charset) up to 32 bytes
#   - value string up to 256 bytes (for setxattr)
#   - one u32 for flags/size
#  For lowlevel notify inval/expire/delete:
#   - parent u64 (and child u64 for delete)
#   - entry name (no '/' and printable, <=255)
#
# We bundle several variants so that different FUZZ_PARAM_* pulls obtain
# suitable data without relying on mutation.

ALNUM_ID_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_.-"
PRINTABLE_NAME_CHARS = ''.join(ch for ch in (string.printable) if ch not in "\x0b\x0c\n\r\t\x0b\x0c/")

def _le32(v: int) -> bytes:
    return int(v & 0xFFFFFFFF).to_bytes(4, 'little')

def _le64(v: int) -> bytes:
    return int(v & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF).to_bytes(8, 'little')

def _tag(tag: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([tag & 0xFF])

def _str_field(s: str) -> bytes:
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    if len(b) > 0xFFFF:
        b = b[:0xFFFF]
    return _tag(0x01) + len(b).to_bytes(2, 'little') + b

def _u32_field(v: int) -> bytes:
    return _tag(0x02) + _le32(v)

def _u64_field(v: int) -> bytes:
    return _tag(0x03) + _le64(v)

def _rand_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Valid non-empty path; keep simple to be widely accepted by FS code
    # Produce variants: root, single component, multi-component
    components: List[str] = []
    ncomp = r.choice([1, 1, 2, 3])
    for i in range(ncomp):
        clen = r.randint(1, 12)
        comp = ''.join(r.choice(ALNUM_ID_CHARS) for _ in range(clen))
        components.append(comp)
    path = "/" + "/".join(components)
    return path

def _rand_xattr_tail(r: random.Random, max_len: int = 32) -> str:
    n = r.randint(1, max_len)
    return ''.join(r.choice(ALNUM_ID_CHARS) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_value(r: random.Random, max_len: int = 256) -> bytes:
    # Value can be arbitrary; prefer printable for readability but allow full byte range
    n = r.randint(1, max_len)
    # Mix of printable and random bytes
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        return bytes(''.join(r.choice(string.printable[:-6]) for _ in range(n)), 'utf-8', 'ignore')
    else:
        return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_dir_name(r: random.Random) -> str:
    n = r.randint(1, 20)
    # Exclude '/' and control chars; keep <=255 by construction
    s = ''.join(r.choice(PRINTABLE_NAME_CHARS) for _ in range(n))
    # Ensure not empty and no '/'
    s = s.replace('/', '')
    if not s:
        s = 'n'
    return s[:255]

def _rand_u64(r: random.Random) -> int:
    # Favor small, large, and edge values
    choices = [0, 1, 2, 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF,
               r.getrandbits(16), r.getrandbits(32), r.getrandbits(64)]
    return r.choice(choices)

def _rand_u32(r: random.Random) -> int:
    choices = [0, 1, 2, 3, 255, 256, 0xFFFFFFFF, r.getrandbits(16), r.getrandbits(32)]
    return choices[r.randrange(len(choices))] & 0xFFFFFFFF

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    fields: List[bytes] = []

    # Bundle for fuse_fs_setxattr
    path1 = _rand_path(r)
    xname1 = _rand_xattr_tail(r, 32)
    val1 = _rand_value(r, 256)
    flags1 = _rand_u32(r) & 0x3  # per stub, mask to low bits
    fields.append(_str_field(path1))
    fields.append(_str_field(xname1))
    fields.append(_str_field(val1.decode('utf-8', 'ignore') if r.random() < 0.8 else val1.hex()))
    fields.append(_u32_field(flags1))

    # Bundle for fuse_fs_getxattr
    path2 = _rand_path(r)
    xname2 = _rand_xattr_tail(r, 32)
    size2 = _rand_u32(r) % 256
    fields.append(_str_field(path2))
    fields.append(_str_field(xname2))
    fields.append(_u32_field(size2))

    # Bundle for fuse_fs_removexattr
    path3 = _rand_path(r)
    xname3 = _rand_xattr_tail(r, 32)
    fields.append(_str_field(path3))
    fields.append(_str_field(xname3))

    # For lowlevel notify_inval_entry and expire_entry
    parent1 = _rand_u64(r)
    name1 = _rand_dir_name(r)
    parent2 = _rand_u64(r)
    name2 = _rand_dir_name(r)
    fields.append(_u64_field(parent1))
    fields.append(_str_field(name1))
    fields.append(_u64_field(parent2))
    fields.append(_str_field(name2))

    # For lowlevel notify_delete
    parent3 = _rand_u64(r)
    child3 = _rand_u64(r)
    name3 = _rand_dir_name(r)
    fields.append(_u64_field(parent3))
    fields.append(_u64_field(child3))
    fields.append(_str_field(name3))

    # Add some extra generic items to supply additional FUZZ_PARAM_STR / UINT pulls
    extra_strs = [
        _rand_dir_name(r),
        _rand_xattr_tail(r, 16),
        _rand_path(r),
    ]
    for s in extra_strs:
        fields.append(_str_field(s))
    for _ in range(3):
        fields.append(_u32_field(_rand_u32(r)))
        fields.append(_u64_field(_rand_u64(r)))

    # Assemble buffer
    # Limit to 4096 bytes
    out = bytearray()
    # Placeholder for count
    out.extend(_le32(0))
    count = 0
    for f in fields:
        if len(out) + len(f) > 4096:
            break
        out.extend(f)
        count += 1
    # Write count
    out[0:4] = _le32(count)
    return bytes(out)
